tasks.short: Collect labour-market benchmarks for hiring, retention and training at our three sites.

today.trigger: A regular benchmark update or a question from the HR Director about labour availability.
steps: Check industry reports, public statistics and staffing-agency reports.
Extract relevant figures into Excel with source dates and definitions.
Compare regions, occupations and permanent versus flex workers.
Resolve incompatible definitions and missing coverage.
Share a short source pack with HR and recruitment.
drudgery: Reopening the same sources to find changes.
Copying tables and recording publication dates.
Discovering late that benchmarks use different populations.
today.time_sinks: Finding comparable figures for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, then checking whether they include flex workers.

lenses.faster: Scheduled collection removes repeated searching and copying; a model extracts figures into a fixed source table. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 24 minutes for checking definitions, resolving gaps and routine upkeep, saving 60%.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly schedule collects available documents from an approved source list and drafts the update. I approve the figures and comparisons before the pack is used.
lenses.ambitious: New service to the two Recruiters: a weekly regional labour-availability brief for hard-to-fill shift roles. Demand would likely grow if a brief became cheap enough to support active vacancy planning.
lenses.joy: I would drop repeated downloading and copying, and spend more time explaining why a local benchmark does or does not fit Noordhaven.
lenses.options: Separate regional, occupation and employment-type comparisons can change whether recruiters widen the search area, change channels or revisit an offer.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts towards assessing source quality and interpreting local differences. I gain delegated authority to exclude unsuitable benchmarks, and the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's initial labour-market research for vacancy planning; learn recruitment-channel economics and local agency coverage.

tasks.human_edge: I recognise when a benchmark's occupation, region or employment conditions make it misleading for a particular Noordhaven vacancy.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: approved documents pass through one extraction call into a checkable table; scheduling and retrieval use fixed software steps.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly benchmark refresh or a new approved source document.
steps: Retrieve accessible documents from the maintained source list; queue portal-only documents for manual upload.
Extract figures, units, populations, dates and supporting passages into a fixed schema.
Flag missing definitions, conflicting figures and changed coverage.
Draft the regional comparison with links to the underlying documents.
Present the pack for analyst approval before publication.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst verifies consequential figures against their sources and approves comparability; missing evidence prevents publication of that comparison.
data_needed: Approved source list and access conditions
Definitions separating employees and flex workers
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint benchmark register containing source versions, extracted passages, corrections and approval.

evidence.claim: A fixed document-extraction workflow can draft structured benchmark records, but source comparability requires review.
The cited Workday workforce report acknowledges that its customer data cannot establish how much of a decline AI caused; benchmark packs should preserve such caveats.

risks: Figures may describe national office employment rather than local warehouse and transport roles.
Purchased sources or agency portals may restrict automated retrieval and reuse.
Extraction errors can make different periods or populations appear comparable.
research_questions: Which sources permit reliable scheduled retrieval, and how much collection still needs manual portal work?
Can extracted figures and definitions match analyst-checked records across representative source formats?
Would recruiters change a vacancy decision after receiving this brief?

tasks.short: Tell HR and managers what changed in our reports, tools and metric definitions.

today.trigger: A dashboard release, corrected measure, access change or new reporting feature.
steps: Review the change and identify affected users.
Write an explanation of the change and its practical effect.
Update report guidance and the metric glossary.
Post or send the announcement.
Answer follow-up questions and correct misunderstandings.
drudgery: Rewriting technical changes for several audiences.
Updating the same explanation in several places.
Answering questions already covered in guidance.
today.time_sinks: Working out who needs to act and keeping announcements consistent with the published report.

lenses.faster: A model drafts audience-specific announcements and guidance from the approved release record. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 27 minutes for checking implications, approving distribution and answering difficult questions, saving 55%.
lenses.autonomous: An approved release starts drafting and prepares the affected audience list. I approve the wording and recipients before software publishes it.
lenses.ambitious: Group served for the first time: night-shift supervisors receive concise Dutch updates explaining which staffing figures changed and what action is needed. Demand would likely grow if useful updates required little extra effort.
lenses.joy: I would lose repetitive announcement writing and spend more time helping managers interpret changes correctly.
lenses.options: Drafts that separate an information-only update from a required action can change the rollout decision, including whether training is needed before release.
lenses.altitude: My week includes more adoption checks and fewer repeated explanations. I gain delegated authority to require user guidance before a report release, making the role more expert in change adoption.
reach: Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's first draft of reporting-tool guidance; learn adult learning and how shift supervisors access material.

tasks.human_edge: I know when a small technical change will undermine trust, alter a manager's decision or require a direct conversation.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one call turns an approved change record into checkable communications within a fixed release workflow.

in_practice.trigger: A report owner marks a release record approved.
steps: Read the approved change record and current guidance.
Determine affected audiences from the maintained report ownership and access register.
Draft Dutch announcements, guidance edits and likely questions.
Present wording, links and recipients for analyst approval.
Publish approved material and record unresolved questions.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the meaning, audience and timing; changes affecting employment policy also require the policy owner's approval.
data_needed: Communication templates and shift access arrangements
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint release register with drafts, approvals, published links and audience.

evidence.claim: A model can draft release communications from supplied facts, with human checking of meaning and recipients.
Power BI Copilot can summarise reports; this supports drafting explanations but does not demonstrate automated change communication.

risks: A fluent announcement may misstate how a measure or access rule changed.
Office-only communication channels may miss shift supervisors.
Examples or screenshots may expose restricted employee information.
research_questions: Are release records complete enough to generate accurate announcements without further interviews?
Which channels actually reach supervisors on all shifts and sites?
Do approved drafts reduce follow-up questions without increasing misunderstanding?

tasks.short: Specify HR dashboards so developers and managers agree on the numbers and access.

today.trigger: A new dashboard request or a material change to an existing report.
steps: Discuss the decision the requester needs to make.
Locate source fields and agree metric definitions.
Specify filters, populations, refresh timing and access.
Write examples and acceptance criteria.
Review the specification with the requester and implementer.
drudgery: Copying field definitions into documents.
Writing repetitive filter and access sections.
Reconciling specifications with the implemented dashboard.
today.time_sinks: Settling definitions such as productive at day 90, retained, onboarding complete and whether flex workers belong in a denominator.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts field mappings, standard sections and acceptance examples from approved definitions. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 33 minutes for requirements discussion, semantic decisions and review, saving 45%.
lenses.autonomous: A dashboard request starts a draft specification and a list of unanswered questions. I lead the discussion and agree the final specification with its business owner.
lenses.ambitious: New service to the HR Director: a specification connecting hiring, week-one onboarding and day-90 outcomes across sites. Demand would grow if cross-system reporting became cheaper to define and maintain.
lenses.joy: I would drop repeated boilerplate and spend more time resolving what managers actually need to know.
lenses.options: Alternative cohort definitions and dashboard layouts reveal different decisions; comparing them can change which measure becomes the agreed North Star.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts towards designing measures and negotiating their business meaning. I gain delegated approval of technical metric definitions and access requirements, while business owners approve employment decisions; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the HR Business Partner's initial translation of management questions into reporting requirements; learn site operations and workforce planning.
Absorb the FP&A Analyst's workforce-report specification work; learn headcount, FTE and labour-cost reconciliation.

tasks.human_edge: I distinguish a measurable proxy from the outcome Noordhaven actually values and negotiate definitions that managers can defend.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the specification depends on discussion and contested definitions; AI helps write and check it while the analyst leads.

in_practice.trigger: A requester submits a dashboard or metric change request.
steps: Read the request, approved glossary and available source schema.
Draft mappings, unresolved questions and alternative cohort definitions.
Work through alternatives with the analyst and business owner.
Draft access rules, refresh expectations and acceptance examples.
Check the final specification against the implemented model.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst and business owner approve definitions and acceptance criteria; obtain OR consent before introducing arrangements covered by WOR Article 27.
data_needed: Source schemas and available export fields
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint versioned specifications with definition decisions, owner approval and acceptance results.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot can help write DAX, but Microsoft warns that an unprepared semantic model can lead to misinterpretation.
WOR Article 27 covers relevant arrangements for employee personal data and facilities capable of monitoring presence, behaviour or performance.

risks: Course completion or attendance may be mistaken for productive performance.
Joining systems can produce incorrect cohorts or expose employee-level information.
A new monitoring dashboard may require OR consent and assessment of applicable EU AI Act obligations.
research_questions: Can AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube records be linked accurately using authorised identifiers?
Can managers agree an observable definition of productive at day 90?
Which proposed measures and access arrangements require OR consent or further privacy assessment?

tasks.short: Turn HR trends into practical recommendations for hiring, onboarding and retention.

today.trigger: The monthly HR review or an unexpected change in a North Star input.
steps: Gather hiring, onboarding, retention and absence measures.
Compare sites, cohorts and periods.
Check data quality and plausible alternative explanations.
Discuss findings with HR Business Partners and relevant specialists.
Prepare recommendations and their limitations.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same comparisons.
Writing descriptions of changes already visible in charts.
Chasing explanations for inconsistent figures.
today.time_sinks: Separating a meaningful operational change from seasonality, small cohorts or a changed recording practice.

lenses.faster: Fixed comparisons run automatically and a model drafts a source-linked interpretation with alternative explanations. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 33 minutes for investigating causes, consulting colleagues and approving recommendations, saving 45%.
lenses.autonomous: The completed monthly refresh starts the analysis pack. I approve its interpretation and recommendations before they enter the HR review.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: weekly selection of a site-level onboarding intervention when completion or early retention deteriorates. Demand would grow if evidence arrived cheaply enough to support short operational reviews.
lenses.joy: I would lose repeated chart commentary and spend more time testing whether an intervention actually helps new starters.
lenses.options: Scenarios for induction timing, buddy coverage and certificate scheduling can change the intervention selected by showing costs, coverage and uncertain outcomes.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts towards evaluating interventions and discussing evidence with site managers. I gain authority to recommend trials and define their success measures, while managers approve operational changes; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the HR Business Partner's first preparation of site-level retention reviews; learn operational constraints and evaluation methods.
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's initial analysis of onboarding completion gaps; learn course scheduling and certification requirements.

tasks.human_edge: I challenge causal claims, recognise site context and judge whether a proposed intervention is fair and workable on shifts.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: a fixed, validated analysis pack becomes a draft interpretation and recommendation table; the analyst approves its meaning.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly data validation completes, or an agreed aggregate threshold is crossed.
steps: Calculate approved cohort and site comparisons using fixed measures.
Apply access controls, group suppression and data-quality checks.
Draft findings, alternative explanations and intervention options from the checked results.
Have the analyst investigate material changes with relevant colleagues.
Publish approved recommendations with owners and evaluation dates.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves all interpretations; HR and site managers approve interventions, with OR involvement where required.
data_needed: Agreed cohort and North Star definitions
Absence rates and durations without medical causes
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint analysis and action register with calculation versions, approved findings and subsequent outcomes.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot supports report summaries, but interpretation depends on a prepared semantic model.
Microsoft's HR account explicitly warns that faster access to information does not itself produce better decisions.
GDPR Article 9 restricts health-data processing; absence analysis needs careful limits on its input data.

risks: Recommendations may imply causation from correlations.
Small site or shift cohorts may identify employees.
Absence patterns must not become medical explanations or automated individual employment decisions.
research_questions: Do drafted interpretations preserve uncertainty and avoid unsupported causal claims?
Are weekly cohorts large and timely enough to support useful intervention decisions?
Can a trial establish whether recommended actions improve onboarding or 90-day retention?

tasks.short: Check that HR reports match agreed definitions, access rules and manager needs.

today.trigger: A report release, source change or suspected discrepancy.
steps: Read the specification and identify required checks.
Reconcile report totals with source records.
Test calculations, filters and reporting periods.
Check access and suppressed groups.
Ask representative users to confirm the report supports their decision.
Record defects and retest corrections.
drudgery: Repeating reconciliations after each change.
Manually checking filter combinations.
Collecting screenshots and copying defect evidence.
today.time_sinks: Tracing differences to source timing, denominator rules or access configuration.

lenses.faster: Written checks run automatically and attach failure evidence; user acceptance and unexplained failures remain with me. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 24 minutes for exception analysis, user checks and test maintenance, saving 60%.
lenses.autonomous: Each refresh or proposed release runs the approved regression suite. Passing routine checks are recorded automatically; failures block release and come to me.
lenses.ambitious: New service to the Payroll Specialist: a pre-close check of reporting headcount and employment changes against payroll control totals. Demand would grow if checks prevented late reconciliation work at low cost.
lenses.joy: I would drop repeated arithmetic and screenshots, and spend more time investigating defects that could change a decision.
lenses.options: Tests against alternative denominator and cutoff rules can expose which interpretation the business needs before an ambiguous report is released.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts towards assurance design and investigating exceptions. I gain delegated authority to stop releases that fail agreed controls, and the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Payroll Specialist's initial reconciliation of HR reporting totals to payroll totals; learn payroll cutoffs, retroactive changes and CAO-related classifications.

tasks.human_edge: I decide whether a passing report answers the real management question and whether an exception is acceptable in its business context.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: totals, filters, access expectations and acceptance examples can be encoded as repeatable checks without a model at runtime.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly extract completion or a report release candidate.
steps: Run the approved calculation and source-reconciliation checks.
Test boundary dates, cohort filters and expected access outcomes.
Check group suppression and source freshness.
Record results and block publication when required checks fail.
Route failures to the analyst and request user acceptance for material changes.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves new test expectations and resolves exceptions; representative users approve material changes to report usefulness.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint test register with dataset and report versions, results, defects and exception approvals.

evidence.claim: Written data reconciliations and regression checks can run deterministically; manager acceptance remains a separate judgement.
Uber's QueryGPT reduced query preparation time, but hallucinated tables and columns remained a problem; generated test code still needs schema and result checks.

risks: A test suite can faithfully enforce an incorrect business definition.
Incomplete access tests may miss exposure of restricted data.
Source and report extracts taken at different times may produce false failures.
research_questions: Which recurring checks can be expressed as stable expected results?
Can the suite catch known historical defects, including access and cutoff errors?
How much exception and maintenance work remains after several refresh and release cycles?

tasks.short: Compare other employers' hiring offers and channels with our results in each region.

today.trigger: Difficulty filling a role, falling offer acceptance or a periodic recruitment-market review.
steps: Collect public vacancies, employer offers and agency market updates.
Compare pay descriptions, shifts, benefits and recruitment channels.
Check comparability with Noordhaven's CAOs and job requirements.
Relate market signals to Recruitee funnel results.
Discuss possible changes with recruitment and compensation colleagues.
drudgery: Copying public vacancy details into comparison sheets.
Separating base pay from allowances and promotional claims.
Repeating searches for the same occupations and regions.
today.time_sinks: Comparing advertised packages that omit hours, allowances, employment terms or actual hiring results.

lenses.faster: Scheduled capture and structured extraction remove much of the search and comparison-sheet work. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 30 minutes for package comparability, interpretation and specialist discussion, saving 50%.
lenses.autonomous: A fortnightly schedule processes approved public sources and agency updates. I approve the comparison and proposed implications before colleagues use it.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: fortnightly review of recruitment-channel allocation for hard-to-fill warehouse and transport roles. Demand would likely grow if credible local comparisons were inexpensive.
lenses.joy: I would drop vacancy copying and spend more time understanding which parts of our offer matter to applicants.
lenses.options: Scenarios for recruitment channels, shift patterns and permitted allowance changes can alter the chosen response by separating acquisition cost from employment cost.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts towards interpreting labour competition and evaluating recruitment experiments. I gain authority to recommend evidence-based channel trials, while recruitment and compensation owners approve spending and terms; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's initial competitor-vacancy comparison; learn channel performance and candidate motivations.
Absorb the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's initial public-offer comparison; learn both applicable CAOs and total reward calculations.

tasks.human_edge: I judge whether advertised terms are comparable and whether a response fits Noordhaven's labour relations and operational needs.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one extraction call converts approved vacancy material into a comparison table; interpretation and action stay behind an analyst gate.

in_practice.trigger: Fortnightly review date or an approved hard-to-fill vacancy request.
steps: Collect permitted public vacancy material and approved agency updates.
Extract stated pay, allowances, hours, location, requirements and source date.
Flag omissions and compare packages using approved calculation rules.
Combine the comparison with validated aggregate recruitment-funnel results.
Present options to the analyst for discussion with recruitment and compensation owners.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst verifies source claims and comparability; the Recruiter and Compensation and Benefits Specialist approve changes within their authority.
data_needed: Applicable CAO pay and allowance rules
Aggregate channel, acceptance and hiring outcomes
Channel costs and approved scenario assumptions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint labour-market comparison register with dated sources, missing terms, calculations and approved recommendations.

evidence.claim: Models can extract stated vacancy terms into a fixed schema, but public advertisements do not establish actual hiring success.
The digest provides no documented Dutch case showing that automated employer comparisons improve recruitment outcomes.

risks: Advertised pay may omit allowances, hours or qualifying conditions.
Public vacancies are a biased sample and do not show competitors' actual acceptance or retention.
Recommendations may conflict with CAO requirements or require consultation on changes to employment arrangements.
research_questions: Do available advertisements contain enough information for meaningful package comparisons?
Can approved rules distinguish base pay, shift allowances and total employment cost?
Would comparison-led channel trials improve productive, retained hires rather than just application volume?

tasks.short: Prepare required workforce reports and reconcile them with our HR records.

today.trigger: A reporting deadline or an authorised request for a required workforce return.
steps: Confirm the recipient, reporting period and required definitions.
Extract relevant employment records from AFAS.
Calculate measures and reconcile totals.
Resolve discrepancies with HR administration or payroll.
Prepare the required format and obtain sign-off.
Submit through the authorised process and archive the evidence.
drudgery: Recreating standard reporting tables.
Reformatting data into recurring templates.
Repeating reconciliation and evidence assembly.
today.time_sinks: Checking reporting cutoffs, employee classifications and whether the nightly extract is current enough for the deadline.

lenses.faster: Versioned rules produce the return, reconciliations and exception list without manual copying. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 21 minutes for resolving exceptions, checking requirements and signing off, saving 65%.
lenses.autonomous: The reporting calendar starts preparation after the relevant source snapshot is available. An authorised person approves every required return before submission.
lenses.ambitious: New service to the Controller: a monthly workforce reconciliation showing how employment movements explain changes in reported FTE and labour costs. Demand would grow if it reduced recurring HR-finance reconciliation effort.
lenses.joy: I would drop template filling and spend more time resolving discrepancies before they reach management or an external recipient.
lenses.options: Alternative cutoff and classification calculations reveal the impact of ambiguous requirements; they help the accountable owner select and document the correct interpretation.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts towards reporting assurance and resolving boundary cases. I gain delegated authority to hold a return with unreconciled totals, while the accountable owner retains submission authority; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller's initial reconciliation between HR workforce figures and finance reporting; learn ledger mappings and labour-cost accruals.
Absorb the HR Administrator's preparation of standard workforce-return tables; learn AFAS employment classifications and correction procedures.

tasks.human_edge: I resolve ambiguous obligations and take responsibility for whether the figures accurately represent Noordhaven's workforce.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: recurring definitions, calculations and output formats can be encoded and validated without a model at runtime.

in_practice.trigger: A deadline in the approved reporting calendar and availability of the required source snapshot.
steps: Select the versioned requirement and reporting-period rules.
Create a controlled snapshot and calculate the required tables.
Reconcile totals and route discrepancies to the responsible data owner.
Generate the return and evidence pack after corrections.
Request authorised approval, then submit through the agreed process and archive the receipt.
in_practice.human_gate: The designated HR, payroll or finance owner approves each required return; unresolved material discrepancies block submission.
data_needed: Actual reporting obligations, templates and deadlines
Employment records and source control totals
Payroll or ledger totals where required
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint reporting register with source snapshot, rule version, reconciliation, approval and submission receipt.

evidence.claim: Recurring workforce returns can be generated through fixed calculations and templates; the exact obligations and available AFAS fields need confirmation.
GDPR Article 9 places additional restrictions on health-data processing; required workforce reports must not casually include sickness causes.

risks: Outdated reporting rules can produce consistently incorrect returns.
Nightly extracts may miss corrections relevant to a reporting cutoff.
A recipient may receive more employee or absence detail than the reporting purpose permits.
research_questions: Which required returns does this analyst actually prepare, and who signs each one?
Can approved calculations reproduce previously accepted returns and explain every difference?
Are the source snapshot, correction process and submission interface reliable enough for each deadline?

tasks.short: Keep our HR reporting definitions, templates and reusable analyses current and easy to find.

today.trigger: A report change, updated policy or CAO, or a periodic library review.
steps: Find affected definitions, templates and analysis examples.
Compare them with current reports and approved policies.
Update reusable material and identify obsolete versions.
Ask the relevant owner to verify consequential changes.
Publish the approved version and update links.
drudgery: Finding duplicate and superseded files.
Checking broken links and missing owners.
Repeating the same explanation across templates.
today.time_sinks: Determining which version is authoritative and whether a proposed edit changes a reporting definition or employment policy.

lenses.faster: Automated inventories identify broken links and review dates, while a copilot drafts comparisons and edits. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 33 minutes for semantic review, owner coordination and publication, saving 45%.
lenses.autonomous: An approved change or scheduled review creates a list of affected assets and draft updates. I lead the review and publish only after the relevant owners approve consequential edits.
lenses.ambitious: New service to the three HR Business Partners: a reusable site-review pack with approved measures, interpretation guidance and action templates. Demand would grow if each site review started from reliable material.
lenses.joy: I would drop version hunting and spend more time creating examples that help colleagues use HR evidence well.
lenses.options: Comparing a shared template with site-specific variants can change whether Noordhaven standardises a review or preserves a justified local difference.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts towards maintaining useful analytical knowledge and coaching colleagues. I gain delegated authority to retire duplicate reporting assets and require named owners, while policy owners approve policy content; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's housekeeping of reporting templates; learn document retention and AFAS template dependencies.
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's first draft of reporting guidance examples; learn instructional design and shift accessibility.

tasks.human_edge: I recognise when apparently duplicate material serves a legitimate site or CAO difference and when a wording change alters policy or metric meaning.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: software finds maintenance candidates and AI drafts edits, but the analyst leads decisions about authoritative and reusable content.

in_practice.trigger: An approved report, policy or CAO change, or the scheduled asset review.
steps: Inventory authorised SharePoint assets and check owners, dates and links.
Identify possible duplicates and references to changed definitions.
Draft comparisons and updates using approved source material.
Have the analyst and relevant owners review edits and retirement proposals.
Publish approved versions, update links and archive superseded material under retention rules.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves analytical guidance; HR policy and CAO owners approve their content, and retention owners approve consequential disposal.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint asset register and version history with source references, owner approvals and retirement decisions.

evidence.claim: Library inventories and link checks can be automated, while models can draft document comparisons for human review.
The digest provides no documented case measuring end-to-end savings for this knowledge-library task.

risks: A draft may blend the transport and warehouse CAOs or erase a valid site difference.
Archiving an asset may break dependencies or conflict with retention requirements.
Broad document retrieval may expose confidential personnel material.
research_questions: Are authoritative documents, owners and dependencies identifiable in the current library?
Can proposed updates preserve material differences between CAOs and sites?
Does the revised library reduce search time and the use of obsolete templates?

role.altitude: The role becomes the steward of reliable HR measures and evidence used by managers and reporting tools. The week shifts towards validating day-90 outcomes, resolving cross-system definitions, checking access and evaluating interventions; delegated rights include approving technical definitions, rejecting unsuitable benchmarks and stopping releases with failed controls.
reach: Recruiter: initial regional labour-market and recruitment-channel analysis; learn channel economics and candidate behaviour.
HR Business Partner: preparation of site-level workforce and retention reviews; learn shift operations and intervention evaluation.
Learning and Development Specialist: onboarding-gap analysis and reporting guidance drafts; learn certification rules and instructional design.
Payroll Specialist and Controller: initial workforce-total reconciliations; learn payroll cutoffs, CAO classifications and finance mappings.
HR Administrator: reporting-template preparation and library maintenance; learn record correction, ownership and retention procedures.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover about 539 hours a year. The steady-state estimates release about 287 hours, including review and routine upkeep but excluding initial implementation; this is about 18% of the role's supplied annual workload, not a whole-role saving. New demand, source-access limits, unresolved definitions and approval duties limit further gains; employment decisions, medical interpretation and accountability remain with authorised people.
skills_to_grow: SQL, Power BI semantic modelling, DAX and source reconciliation.
AFAS extract design and authorised Recruitee and Studytube data integration.
Cohort design, uncertainty, causal evaluation and experiment planning.
Dutch CAO interpretation, workforce costing and payroll cutoffs.
AVG/GDPR access design, group suppression and data minimisation.
WOR Article 27 consent processes and assessment of applicable EU AI Act duties and commencement dates.
AI-output verification, source tracing and practical evaluation of time saved.
Requirements negotiation and communication with site and shift managers.
role.ambitious_version: Provide the HR Director and site managers with a trusted weekly view of where hiring fails to become productive, retained employment, including flex workers where agency data and permissions support valid comparison. Connect recruitment, onboarding and day-90 outcomes, offer costed intervention scenarios, and evaluate approved trials; keep absence analysis to authorised rates and durations, establish required OR consent, and measure decisions and outcomes rather than counting AI usage.
